AgentScribe — Implementation Plan\n\n## Overview\n\nAgentScribe is a Rust CLI binary that scrapes conversation logs from multiple coding agent types, normalizes them into a canonical format, and stores them as flat files with a Tantivy search index. It serves three purposes:\n\n1. **Archive** — capture and preserve the full prompt/response history from all agents running in an environment\n2. **Search** — provide a query interface that agents can invoke to find past solutions, error patterns, and reference implementations\n3. **Learn** — distill accumulated agent knowledge into actionable intelligence: error→solution mappings, anti-patterns, project rules, and effectiveness analytics\n\n---\n\n## Problem\n\nEvery coding agent stores its conversation history differently — JSONL, Markdown, JSON trees, SQLite blobs. When multiple agents operate in the same environment, there is no unified way to search across their collective knowledge. A solution one agent found last week is invisible to another agent today. Mistakes are repeated. Patterns go unnoticed. Institutional knowledge is locked inside individual agent log formats.\n\n---\n\n## Agent Log Formats (Known Sources)\n\n### Claude Code\n- **Location:** `~/.claude/projects/<path-encoded>/<session-uuid>.jsonl`\n- **Format:** JSONL, one event per line\n- **Schema:** `{type, uuid, sessionId, timestamp, cwd, version, gitBranch, message: {role, content}}`\n- **Types:** `user`, `assistant`, `progress`, `file-history-snapshot`\n- **Sub-agents:** `<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` (same format, `isSidechain: true`)\n- **Metadata:** `~/.claude/usage-data/session-meta/<session-uuid>.json` (duration, tokens, tool counts)\n- **Summaries:** `~/.claude/usage-data/facets/<session-uuid>.json` (LLM-generated goal/outcome/summary)\n\n### Aider\n- **Location:** `.aider.chat.history.md` in project root\n- **Format:** Markdown, append-only\n- **Schema:** `#### ` prefix = user message, `> ` prefix = tool output, bare text = assistant response\n- **Input history:** `.aider.input.history` (prompt_toolkit format: `# timestamp` + `+` prefixed lines)\n- **Session marker:** `# aider chat started at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` delimits sessions\n\n### OpenCode\n- **Location:** `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/` (legacy JSON) or `.opencode/` (current SQLite)\n- **Format:** Individual JSON files in a hierarchy (legacy) or SQLite via Drizzle ORM (current)\n- **Schema:** `session/{projectId}/{sessionId}.json`, `message/{sessionId}/{messageId}.json`, `part/{messageId}/{partId}.json`\n- **Fields:** role, cost, tokens, timestamps; parts contain text, tool calls, tool results\n\n### Codex (OpenAI)\n- **Location:** `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-{timestamp}-{uuid}.jsonl` (may be `.jsonl.zst`)\n- **Format:** JSONL, one envelope per line: `{timestamp, type, payload}`\n- **Schema:** Line 1 is `type: \"session_meta\"` (`payload: {id, cwd, cli_version, instructions, git}`); subsequent lines are `type: \"response_item\"` (`payload.type: \"message\"` with `role` + `content[]` blocks of `input_text`/`output_text`, or `function_call`/`function_call_output` for tool use), `type: \"turn_context\"` (`payload.model`), and `type: \"event_msg\"` noise\n- **Companion:** `~/.codex/history.jsonl` (cross-session user-prompt history)\n- **Note:** Internal format, subject to change; ephemeral mode writes no file. **The bundled v1.0 plugin maps a flat `{time, role, content}` shape that real rollouts do not use — fixed in Phase 9 via envelope unwrapping.**\n\n### Pi (badlogic/pi-mono)\n- **Location:** `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<path-encoded-project>/<timestamp>-<uuid>.jsonl` (layout mirrors Claude Code: one JSONL file per session, project dir path-encoded)\n- **Format:** JSONL, one event per line; first line is a session header, subsequent lines are messages with `role`/`content` and tool-call records\n- **Note:** No install present on this machine — field names must be verified against a real `~/.pi` tree before the plugin ships (Phase 9 bead includes this verification step)\n\n### Gemini CLI\n- **Location:** `~/.gemini/tmp/<project-hash>/logs.json` (rolling message log) and `~/.gemini/tmp/<project-hash>/chats/*.json` (saved checkpoints)\n- **Format:** Single JSON file containing an **array** of message objects (`{sessionId, messageId, type, message, timestamp}`) — not JSONL; requires the Phase 9 `json-array` format\n- **Note:** Project identity is a hash directory, not a path — project detection needs the checkpoint metadata or falls back to unknown\n\n### Goose\n- **Location:** `~/.local/share/goose/sessions/*.jsonl`\n- **Format:** JSONL; aider sessions.\n\n## Investigation Results\n\n### Aider Analytics Format\n\nFrom aider/analytics.py source, each analytics log entry has this structure:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"event\": \"message_send\",\n  \"properties\": {\n    \"main_model\": \"gpt-4\",\n    \"weak_model\": \"gpt-3.5-turbo\",\n    \"editor_model\": \"gpt-4\",\n    \"total_tokens\": 1234,\n    \"total_cost\": 0.05\n  },\n  \"user_id\": \"uuid-string-for-user\",\n  \"time\": 1710492000\n}\n```\n\n**Key fields:**\n- `event`: Event name (e.g., \"message_send\", \"edit\", etc.)\n- `properties`: Event metadata including model names, tokens, costs\n- `user_id`: Persistent UUID4 user identifier (same across all sessions)\n- `time`: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch, UTC)\n\n### Chat Session Detection\n\nThe aider plugin uses delimiter-based session detection:\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"delimiter\"\ndelimiter_pattern = \"^# aider chat started at \"\n```\n\nExample The `user_id` field is a persistent user identifier, not a per-session ID.\n\n### Problem: Ambiguous Timestamp Correlation\n\nEven if we attempted timestamp-based correlation:\n\n1. **Timezone ambiguity**: Chat delimiter timestamps have no timezone specified, while analytics timestamps are always UTC (Unix epoch). This makes precise matching difficult.\n\n2. **Timestamp mismatch**: The delimiter timestamp (`# aider chat started at 2024-03-15 10:00:00`) represents when the session started, but analytics events occur throughout the session with their own timestamps.\n\n3. **No 1:1 mapping**: Multiple analytics events occur within a single session, and multiple sessions could potentially overlap or have similar timestamps.\n\n4. **Delimiter format**: The delimiter timestamp format is human-readable and potentially inconsistent, making reliable parsing and conversion to Unix timestamps problematic.\n\n### Companion Index Mechanism Requirements\n\nThe companion index mechanism expects:\n- `thread_id` or `session_id` field for keying entries\n- Per-session metadata records\n\nAider analytics provides:\n- `user_id`: Persistent user identifier (not session-specific)\n- `time`: Event timestamp (not session ID)\n\n**Result:** Analytics data does not meet the structural requirements for companion index correlation.\n\n## Conclusion\n\n**Correlation is NOT feasible.** The aider analytics JSONL file cannot be reliably consumed as a companion index because:\n\n1. **No session identifier**: Analytics events lack a `session_id` or `thread_id` field that can be correlated to chat history sessions\n2. **Persistent user ID only**: The `user_id` field identifies the user across all sessions, not individual sessions\n3. **Ambiguous timestamp matching**: Time-based correlation is unreliable due to timezone ambiguity, format differences, and lack of 1:1 mapping\n\n**Recommendation:** Do NOT wire aider analytics as a companion index. The format varies by import type:\n70\t///\n71\t/// - **For `use` statements**: Full module path being imported (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`,\n72\t///   `\"crate::module::Item\"`, `\"super::ParentModule\"`)\n73\t/// - **For `extern crate`**: The crate name (e.g., `\"serde\"`, `\"tokio\"`)\n74\t/// - **For `mod`**: The module name (e.g., `\"foo\"`, `\"bar\"`)\n75\t///\n76\t/// **Constraints:**\n77\t/// - Non-empty string (cannot be `\"\"`)\n78\t/// - Contains only valid Rust identifier characters and path separators (`::`)\n79\t/// - Case-sensitive (matches Rust's rules)\n80\t///\n81\t/// **Usage in practice:**\n82\t/// ```rust\n83\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n84\t///\n85\t/// // Standard library import\n86\t/// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n87\t///\n88\t/// // Crate-relative import\n89\t/// let crate_import = Import::new(\"crate::module::Item\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n90\t///\n91\t/// // External crate\n92\t/// let extern_import = Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n93\t/// ```\n94\t///\n95\t/// ## `import_type: ImportType`\n96\t///\n97\t/// The type classification of the import statement. JSON using dot notation\n440\tpub fn extract_field(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n441\t    if path.is_empty() {\n442\t        return None;\n443\t    }\n444\t\n445\t    let mut current = value;\n446\t    for part in path.split('.') {\n447\t        // Handle array indexing like parts[0]\n448\t        if let Some(bracket_pos) = part.find('[') {\n449\t            let key = &part[..bracket_pos];\n450\t            let index_str = &part[bracket_pos + 1..part.len() - 1];\n451\t            let index: usize = index_str.parse().ok()?;\n452\t\n453\t            current = extract_string(value, path)\n476\t        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n477\t\n478\t    // Try ISO 8601 first\n479\t    if let Ok(dt) = timestamp\".to_string()));\n493\t    }\n494\t\n495\t    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n496\t    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n497\t        return Ok(dt);\n498\t          })\n581\t                .collect();\n582\t            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n583\t                None\n584\t            } else {\n585\t                Some(text_parts.join(\" \"))\n586\t            }\n587\t        }\n588\t        _ => None,\n589\t    }\n590\t}\n591\t\n592\t/// Parse a timestamp from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n593\t///\n594\t/// Wrapper around `extract_string_with_envelope` that parses the extracted string\n595\t/// as a timestamp. Supports ISO 8601, Unix epoch (seconds/milliseconds), and\n596\t/// UTC-naive formats.\n597\tpub fn parse_timestamp_with_envelope(\n598\t    path: &str,\n599\t    payload: &Value,\n600\t    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n601\t) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n602\t    let ts_str = extract_string_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)\n603\t        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n604\t\n605\t    // Try ISO 8601 first\n606\t    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n607\t        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n608\t    }\n609\t\n610\t    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n611\t    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n612\t        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n613\t            // Milliseconds\n614\t            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n615\t        } else {\n616\t            // Seconds\n617\t            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n618\t        };\n619\t        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n620\t    }\n621\t\n622\t    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n623\t    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n624\t        return Ok(dt);\n625\t    }\n626\t\n627\t    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n628\t        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n629\t        ts_str\n630\t    )))\n631\t}\n632\t\n633\t/// Base trait for all format parsers\n634\tpub trait FormatParser {\n635\t    /// Parse events from the source\n636\t    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n637\t\n638\t    /// Parse events from the source, starting from a given byte offset for incremental parsing.\n639\t    ///\n640\t    /// For formats that support incremental parsing (JSONL, append-only logs), this allows\n641\t    /// the parser to skip already-processed content and only parse new data.\n642\t    ///\n643\t    /// # Arguments\n644\t    ///\n645\t    /// * `source_path` - Path to the source file\n646\t    /// * `plugin` - Plugin configuration for this source\n647\t    /// * `start_offset` - Byte offset to start reading from (0 for full parse)\n648\t    ///\n649\t    /// # Returns\n650\t    ///\n651\t    /// - `Ok(events)` - Vector of parsed events\n652\t    /// - `Err(_)` - Parse error (check `is_skippable()` for non-fatal errors)\n653\t    fn parse_incremental(\n654\t        &self,\n655\t        source_path: &Path,\n656\t        plugin: &Plugin,\n657\t        start_offset: u64,\n658\t    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n659\t        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n660\t        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n661\t        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n662\t    }\n663\t\n664\t    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n665\t    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n666\t}\n667\t\n668\t/// Information about a detected session\n669\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n670\t#[allow(dead_code)]\n671\tpub struct SessionInfo {\n672\t    pub session_id: String,\n673\t    pub start_offset: u64,\n674\t    pub end_offset: u64,\n675\t    pub metadata: Option<Value>,\n676\t    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n677\t    /// is a child of another session)\n678\t    pub parent_session_id: Option<String>,\n679\t}\n680\t\n681\t#[cfg(test)]\n682\tmod tests {\n683\t    use super::*;\n684\t    use serde_json::json;\n685\t\n686\t    // Tests for Import and ImportType plugin: &Plugin,\n        start_offset: u64,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n    }\n\n    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n}\n\n///      // Unicode and special characters\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^_field\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^$field\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^field-name\"));\n It:\n\n- Loads JSONL files containing per-session metadata\n- Keys entries by `thread_id` or `session_id` fields\n- Returns metadata for a given session ID via `CompanionIndex::get(session_id)`\n\n**Expected structure:**\n```json\n{\"thread_id\": \"abc123\", \"model\": \"gpt-4\", \"cwd\": \"/home/user/project\"}\n{\"thread_id\": \"def456\", \"model\": \"gpt-3.5-turbo\", \"cwd\": \"/home/user/other\"}\n```\n\n### Requirements\n\nThe companion index mechanism requires:\n- **Per-session keys:** Each entry must have a `thread_id` or `session_id` field\n- **1:1 mapping:** One metadata record per session\n- **Direct lookup:** Session ID → metadata via hash map lookup\n\n---\n\n## Aider Analytics Structure\n\n### Format\n\nFrom `aider/analytics.py`, each analytics event has:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"event\": \"message_send\",\n  \"properties\": {\n    \"main_model\": \"gpt-4\",\n    \"weak_model\": \"gpt-3.5-turbo\",\n    \"total_tokens\": 1234,\n    \"total_cost\": 0.05\n  },\n  \"user_id\": \"uuid-string-for-user\",\n  \"time\": 1710492000\n}\n```\n\n**Key fields:**\n- `user_id`: Persistent UUID4 identifying the user across ALL sessions\n- `time`: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch, UTC)\n- `properties`: Event metadata (model, tokens, cost)\n\n### What's Missing\n\n**No session identifier exists.** The analytics file contains:\n- `user_id`: Global user identifier (same value in every event)\n- `time`: Event timestamp (not a session ID)\n\nThere is NO field that uniquely identifies a session or can be used as a foreign key to chat history.\n\n---\n\n## AgentScribe Aider Session Detection\n\n### Delimiter-Based Detection\n\nThe Aider plugin uses delimiter-based session detection (`plugins/aider.toml`):\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"delimiter\"\ndelimiter_pattern = \"^# aider chat started at \"\n```\n\n### Session ID Generation\n\nFrom `src/parser/markdown.rs::detect_sessions()`:\n\n1. Split file by delimiter lines: `# aider chat started at 2024-03-15 10:00:00`\n2. Generate session IDs: `{filename}-{session_num}`\n   - Example: `.aider.chat.history.md-0`, `.aider.chat.history.md-1`\n3. Extract timestamp from delimiter (human-readable format)\n\n### Session Metadata\n\n**Delimiter format:**\n```\n# aider chat started at 2024-03-15 10:00:00\n```\n\n**Problems:**\n- No timezone specified (local time? UTC?)\n- Human-readable format (not easily parsed)\n- No session ID or thread ID\n- Timestamp represents session start, not individual events\n\n---\n\n## Correlation Attempts\n\n### 1. Direct Session Key Lookup\n\n**Attempt:** Use `user_id` as session identifier\n\n**Problem:** `user_id` is persistent across ALL sessions. Every analytics event from the same user has the same `user_id`. There is no per-session granularity.\n\n**Result:** ❌ NOT FEASIBLE - Cannot distinguish between sessions\n\n---\n\n### 2. Timestamp Overlap Matching\n\n**Attempt:** Correlate delimiter timestamps with analytics event timestamps\n\n**Problems:**\n\n1. **Timezone ambiguity**\n   - Delimiter: `2024-03-15 10:00:00` (no timezone)\n   - Analytics: `1710492000` (UTC Unix timestamp)\n   - Cannot reliably match without knowing the delimiter's timezone\n\n2. **No 1:1 mapping**\n   - One delimiter = session start\n   - Multiple analytics events per session (each message is an event)\n   - Cannot determine which delimiter corresponds to which event sequence\n\n3. **Timestamp format inconsistency**\n   - Delimiter timestamps are human-readable and potentially inconsistent\n   - Analytics timestamps are precise Unix epochs\n   - Parsing delimiter timestamps is unreliable\n\n4. **Session boundary ambiguity**\n   - Sessions detected by delimiter position in file\n   - Analytics events have independent timestamps\n   - No clear way to map event sequences to delimiter ranges\n\n**Result:** ❌ NOT FEASIBLE - Too much ambiguity for reliable correlation\n\n---\n\n### 3. Hybrid Approach (User ID + Time Window)\n\n**Attempt:** Combine `user_id` with approximate time windows\n\n**Problems:**\n\n1. **User ID adds no value** - Same user ID for all sessions from same user\n2. **Time windows are ambiguous** - Same timezone problems as timestamp overlap\n3. **Multiple sessions could overlap** - Sessions can be concurrent or overlapping in time\n\n**Result:** ❌ NOT FEASIBLE - User ID doesn't reduce ambiguity\n\n---\n\n## Structural Incompatibility Summary\n\n| Aspect | Aider Chat History | Aider Analytics | Compatible? |\n|--------|-------------------|-----------------|--------------|\n| **Session identifier** | Delimiter position | None | ❌ NO |\n| **User identifier** | None | `user_id` (global) | ❌ NO (different scopes) |\n| **Timestamp format** | Human-readable (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`) | Unix epoch (UTC) | ⚠️ AMBIGUOUS |\n| **Timezone** | Not specified | UTC | ❌ NO |\n| **Granularity** | Per session | Per event | ❌ NO |\n| **Count** | 1 record per session | N events per session | ❌ NO |\n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\n### Why Correlation Is Not Feasible\n\n1. **No shared session identifier:** Analytics lacks a field that can be used as a foreign key to chat sessions\n2. **User ID is global, not per-session:** `user_id` identifies the user across all sessions, not individual sessions\n3. **Timestamp matching is unreliable:** Timezone ambiguity, format differences, and lack of 1:1 mapping prevent precise correlation\n4. **Structural mismatch:** Chat history is session-based; analytics is event-based with no session grouping\n\n### Recommendation\n\n**Do NOT wire aider analytics as a companion index.** The data structure is fundamentally incompatible with the companion mechanism's session-based keying requirements.\n\nThe documentation in `plugins/aider.toml` correctly identifies this incompatibility:\n\n```toml\n# Companion index decision (bf-xp9w):\n# Aider analytics JSONL (~/.aider.analytics.jsonl) is NOT wired as a companion_index\n# because it lacks session-level identifiers needed for correlation.\n```\n\n### Alternative Approaches\n\nIf analytics metadata (model, tokens, cost) is needed for aider sessions:\n\n1. **Add session IDs to analytics:** Modify aider to emit a session identifier in analytics events\n2. **Separate metadata file:** Create a companion file that explicitly maps session IDs to metadata\n3. **Post-scrape enrichment:** Use project, timestamp heuristics, or user input to backfill metadata\n\n---\n\n## Related Documentation\n\n- **Full analysis:** `notes/bf-xp9w.md` - aider analytics companion evaluation\n- **Plugin config:** `plugins/aider.toml` - Aider plugin with companion index decision\n- **Companion implementation:** `src/scraper/companion.rs` - Companion index mechanism\n- **Session detection:** `src/parser/markdown.rs` - Delimiter-based session detection\n\n---\n\n**Status:** ✅ Analysis complete - Correlation confirmed as NOT feasible  \n**Next steps:** None - This bead can be closed with documented infeasibility\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8d85b798-c140-4771-909b-a5f129c5ea08","uuid":"f8a128c0-7d7d-4950-ac67-d01f6a5005ce","timestamp":"2026-08-16T17:57:13.899Z"}
